chunks: Remember when Moses said to his people: 'O my people, remember the favours that God bestowed on you when He appointed apostles from among you, and made you kings and gave you what had never been given to any one in the world.'

key_terms.إِذْ: When (referring to a specific past time or event)

ai.seo_question: What three specific favors did God bestow upon the Children of Israel according to this verse?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to affirm the legitimacy of political authority (mulk) alongside prophethood (nubuwwah) as dual divine blessings for the Children of Israel, a theme that resonates with the concept of Imamate as both spiritual and temporal guidance. The mention of 'kingship' is interpreted by scholars like Al-Tabarsi and Al-Tusi as referring to the lineage of Saul (Talut) and David (Dawud), establishing a precedent for divinely sanctioned leadership. This dual bestowal underscores the completeness of God's favor, which the Israelites later squandered through disobedience.
